items.title: Thunderscan: A clever device transforms a printer into a scanner (2004)
items.raw_content: The first project that I worked on for Apple after starting in August 1979 was writing low level software for the Silentype printer (see What Hath Woz Wrought ) , a cute, inexpensive thermal printer for the Apple II, that was based on technology licensed from a local company named Trendcom. In typical Apple fashion, we improved on Trendcom's design by replacing their relatively expensive controller board with a much simpler one that relied on the microprocessor in the Apple II to do most of the dirty work.
items.title_zh: Thunderscan：把打印机变成扫描仪的巧妙设备（2004）

items.title: NSA and IETF: Can an attacker purchase standardization of weakened cryptography?
items.raw_content: It's normal for post-quantum cryptography to be rolled out as an extra layer of security on top of traditional pre-quantum cryptography, rather than as a replacement . For example, Google's CECPQ1 experiment was double encryption with traditional pre-quantum ECC (specifically X25519 ) and post-quantum NewHope1024. CECPQ2 , a joint experiment between Google and Cloudflare, was ECC+NTRUHRSS701. CECPQ2b was ECC+SIKEp434. Ten SSH implementations support ECC+sntrup761. Today's usage of post-quantum cryptography by browsers is approaching half of the connections seen by Cloudflare, where 95% of that is ECC+MLKEM768 and 5% is ECC+Kyber768.
items.title_zh: NSA 与 IETF：攻击者能否买通弱化加密的标准化？
items.summary: A cryptography blog post asks whether an attacker can buy standardization of weakened cryptography, noting that post-quantum algorithms are typically deployed as an extra layer over traditional cryptography in browsers and SSH.
